comments.author: @BoydXplorer
comments.text: Saint Basil’s Cathedral on Moscow’s Red Square is a 16th-century Russian architectural masterpiece. Famous for its vibrant, flame-like multicolored onion domes and labyrinthine interior of interconnected chapels, it was built by Ivan the Terrible between 1555 and 1561 to celebrate a historic military victory. It features a unique cluster of nine main chapels grouped around a central church, styled to resemble a bonfire reaching toward the sky. Its exterior facade is bright geometric patterns, rich redbrick walls, and bulbous domes in vivid shades of green, blue, yellow, and red.Interior: A cozy, maze-like network of narrow vaulted corridors, shadowy galleries, and ancient walls painted with 16th- to 17th-century floral and religious frescoes. Officially named the Cathedral of the Intercession of the Holy Virgin on the Moat, it later took the name of Basil the Blessed, a local holy saint buried on the site. Thanks for the tour. I enjoyed the virtual cityscape of Russia.

replies.text: St. Basil’s Cathedral really is one of those buildings you recognize instantly. The colors and unusual domes make it unlike almost anything else in Moscow. Which part fascinates you most—the architecture, its history under Ivan the Terrible, or the interior chapels?
